commit.message:
feat(import): read SolidCraft face names beside the .sc final body

The Solidcraft reader reads the name of each record face of the final
body from model cache format 10 (`model.names[model_bodies[m].names]`:
`faces` and the `verified` and `former` items of `info`). One name for
each record face, in record order. A cache of another format gives no
names and no note. Names that do not fit the body give no names and one
note; they never refuse the import.

Pins: names read with four- and five-item info; every triangle of a
named face lies on that face's plane (a block of our own, with a shifted
list as the negative control); each misfit gives a note; format 8 reads
none; the SolidCraft-written hole_on_pocket_wall.sc names its caps in
record order; hostile names records never panic or refuse.

Built and tested on the earlier base 773736856 (the PR body lists the
runs). Rebased onto a721fd4dc without a local build; the maintainer's
runners test it.

Refs #3915

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(import): hold the .sc face names beside the model's facets

The Solidcraft import builds facet ranges from the machining mesh's
`tri_face` (one range for each run of a record face) and hands them out
with SolidCraft's names as `geometry::source_faces::SourceFaces`, beside
the mesh. A record that does not tile the facets is dropped with a note.

In the app, `Graded` and `ImportModel` carry it, and a new component
(`schema::SourceFaces`, through `source_faces::{of, set}`) holds it on
the model in memory only. It keeps the revision and facet count it was
landed with, so any other landing of facets makes it stale. UpdateModel
trades it on undo (`with_source_faces`); unstated, an update drops it,
so a repair or a file that is not `.sc` drops the names. DeleteEntity
puts it back on undo. The window, script/MCP import and fixture
re-import pass it. Nothing reads it yet and the project file is
unchanged: no behaviour change.

Built and tested on the earlier base 773736856 (the PR body lists the
runs). Rebased onto a721fd4dc without a local build; the maintainer's
runners test it.

test(import): pin the .sc face names in the document; record D1-D3

App pins (crates/app/tests/import_solidcraft/source_faces.rs, joined
to the import_solidcraft binary): a format-10 `.sc` import lands its
names with the facets (undo and redo); STL, OBJ and STEP models have
none; an update trades the names on undo and drops them when it does
not state them; a repair drops them and undo brings them back; a
deleted model comes back with them; names that do not tile, or that
other facets landed over, are never handed out.

feat(mcp): import_model answers an update with its feature changes

When import_model updates a model that was there before the call, the
answer gets the optional key `changes`: for the faces, the welded faces
and the edge chains, the carried, added and missing id counts, and the
window's phrase (`FeatureChanges::describe`). The diff is
`revision::changes`, the one `UpdateModel::changes` gives the window.
A first import has no `changes`.

The hook in mcp/tools.rs is four lines. The logic is in the new
mcp/reimport_changes.rs. It keeps each model's facets (Arc) and revision
before the call, then selects the model by the answer's own `model`
name, so script/api.rs (which #4212 and #4213 change) is not touched.

Tests: crates/app/tests/mcp/reimport_changes.rs.
Decision entries: this PR's file in docs/decisions/.

feat(mcp): show SolidCraft face names on features and picks

When a model holds the source face record of a .sc import (#4212),
list_features face and patch rows, and the face and patch picks that
picks_view shows (get_operation_geometry, set_operation_geometry,
get_selection, the area and "Do not touch" views, pick_in_box), get the
optional key `source_name` (one name) or `source_names` (several,
sorted), and `source_unverified: true` when SolidCraft has not verified
one of them. A model with no record, a record that does not tile the
facets, or a pick that is no longer in the model shows no new key.

- camcraft_geometry::geometry::source_names: the name set of a face id
  or a patch, from the record and the mesh's features. No names when the
  record does not fit, never a wrong or partial set.
- app mcp/source_names.rs: finds the record (one call into
  crate::source_faces::of), builds features from the model's own facets
  (the content-keyed caches can answer with another facet order), and
  writes the keys. Hooks: three lines in mcp/features.rs (after the
  compact step, so compact rows keep the names; no work when the call
  lists neither faces nor patches), two in mcp/pick.rs::picks_view.

Uses the record interface of #4212: crate::source_faces::of,
crate::geometry::source_faces::{SourceFaces, FaceName, FacetRange},
SourceFaces::{from_tri_face, tiles, face_of}, and
ImportModel.source_faces (the tests land records through it).

Tests: geometry unit tests in source_names.rs, and
crates/app/tests/mcp/source_names.rs (records on a box and a cylinder
landed through ImportModel, and the format-10 fixture
hole_on_pocket_wall.sc through the real import). New files are
formatted at 120 columns, as the code around them.

test(mcp): fix the .sc pick test's pocket heights

The first run of the test found that set_operation_geometry refused the
2D Pocket of a_sc_import_names_every_face_and_patch: "a 2D Pocket
operation must cut downward: its top height resolves below its bottom
height". The top was "top of stock" over a stock copied from the plate.
The test is about the name on the pick, so the pocket's top is now a
fixed world Z 1 mm above the picked face. The name checks before it
already passed.
